plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one focused S&C session each week. Week 1 establishes a training max for the back squat so later percentage work is grounded in a real baseline, and the main loading starts in Week 2. With only one gym session per week, the session keeps a simple full-body structure: explosive work first, then main strength, then practical upper-back, trunk, and brief neck work.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build lower-body force, full-body power, and trunk strength while keeping the session compact and recoverable around boxing work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Push the main strength work a little heavier and keep power output crisp without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more toward fast, sharp output while holding onto the strength built earlier.

exercises.name: 1a. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on quietly and cleanly. Reset between reps and keep every jump fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if box setup is awkward. Jump for height and stick the landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Trap Bar Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if you are confident with loaded jumps. Keep the load light and the reps crisp.

exercises.name: 1b. Medicine Ball Rotational Scoop Throw
exercises.notes: Throw each rep with full intent from the hips. Use a non-bouncing ball or throw into a solid wall with control on the catch.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Shot Put
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if scoop throw space is limited. Drive hard from the rear hip.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up in steady jumps, then work up to one hard top set with clean depth and no grindy spotter-assisted reps.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can set your future squat percentages.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean 3-5 rep set with solid depth and bar speed.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if back squat setup is not available or your shoulders tolerate front rack better.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if available and it lets you squat hard with better comfort.

exercises.name: 3a. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Drive the elbows back and pause briefly at the top. Keep the torso still and stop before form slips.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the chest-supported station is busy. Keep the trunk braced and pull to the hip.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simpler setup with steady tension.

exercises.name: 3b. Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Reach long, keep ribs down, and stop the range before the low back arches.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no ab wheel is available.

substitutionOptions.name: Hanging Knee Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if rollout position bothers the shoulders.

exercises.name: 4. Plate Neck Flexion and Extension
exercises.notes: Use very light load, move slowly, and keep it smooth. Stop if you feel any sharp discomfort.

substitutionOptions.name: Neck Harness Extension and Supine Neck Flexion
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if that setup is more comfortable and controlled.
